111	## 4. Permission model
112	
113	1. **What is asked.** Only a call for which the gate computed `askOperator` (dispatch_tool_call.ts:451-455) and then called `onConfirm` (553). That covers:
114	   - a write, exec or egress in review mode
115	   - a first egress per origin in auto mode
116	   - a command rule `prompt`
117	   - a verification edit `ask`
118	   - an injection suspicion
119	   - a re-issued interrupted call
120	2. **What is never asked.** Every denial listed in §1, plus read-only mode and the sandbox inside `spine.execute`. These return a `DENIED` receipt without emitting `approval.request`, so the adapter has no pending entry and sends no `session/request_permission`.
121	3. **Why `allow` cannot override a denial.**
122	   - The reply enters at exactly one place: `SidecarLink.send({type:"approve", id, always:false})` → `resolveApproval` (sidecar.ts:881).
123	   - That resolves only the promise of the one open approval whose id matches; anything else is `NO_PENDING_APPROVAL`.
124	   - After an approval the call still passes `spine.execute` (read-only, sandbox).
125	   - The adapter has no other verb that affects a tool call.
126	4. **Binding.** A registry holds `rpcId → {sessionId, approvalId, turnId, toolCallId, digest, state}`.
127	   - `digest` is the SHA-256 of the canonical `{tool, subject, preview, review}`; it is logged and sent as `toolCall._meta["nexus/approval_digest"]`.
128	   - A reply carries no content, so it can only answer the request that created its `rpcId`.
129	   - Outgoing ids are integers from a random 31-bit start (**NV**: whether clients accept string ids), so a response sent before the request exists matches nothing.
130	5. **Replies that are ignored and logged to stderr, never forwarded.** A tombstone LRU of 256 entries separates stale from unknown.
131	   - unknown `rpcId`
132	   - already answered (a second reply)
133	   - a reply after cancel, turn end or disconnect
134	   - a response whose `id` is that of a client→agent request
135	   - a malformed result
136	6. **Result mapping.**
137	   - `{outcome:"selected", optionId:"allow_once"}` → `approve`.
138	   - Everything else → `deny`: `reject_once`, `cancelled`, an option id not offered (**V[HM permissions.py:98-104]** treats an unknown id as deny), `allow_always`, a JSON-RPC error, a wrong type.
139	   - `always` is the constant `false`. No code path builds `always:true`; a test spies on the link.
140	7. **Defaults.**
141	   - No answer within `--permission-timeout` (default 600 s; **V[HM permissions.py:112]** uses 60 s, which is too short for a person in an editor) → `deny`, and the turn continues.
142	   - Client disconnect, stdin EOF or a signal → shutdown; the sidecar settles the approval false (861).
143	   - `session/cancel` → the sidecar `cancel` settles it false.
144	8. **Cancel race.**
145	   - On `session/cancel` the entry moves to `cancelled` before `cancel` is sent. A later `allow` is stale and ignored.
146	   - The prompt answers `cancelled` only after `turn.result` arrives.
147	   - If the approve reached the sidecar first, the tool runs and the abort signal interrupts it. That is the existing TUI behaviour (`cli/test/sidecar.test.ts:351`).
148	   - The adapter accepts an inbound `$/cancel_request {requestId}` for a prompt request as a cancel (**V[OC turn.ts:390; `packages/cli/test/acp/prompt.test.ts`:495]**).
149	   - It does not send `$/cancel_request` itself until its spec status is confirmed. **NV**: observed only as SDK behaviour, **V[OC `packages/cli/test/acp/permission.test.ts`:140-144]**.
150	9. **Mode and trust come from the operator's machine only.**
151	   - `nexus acp [flags] [-- <sidecar flags>]` forwards operator flags to each child; `-w` and `-r` are refused because the adapter owns them.
152	   - v1.3.0 allows `--mode review` (default) and `--read-only`. `--yes` and `--mode auto` are refused at start-up with a message (D-AC-3).
153	   - Trust is read by the child from the trust store. No protocol field, `_meta` key or `clientInfo` value is read for authority.
154	10. **Untrusted workspace and broken policy.**
155	    - Untrusted `cwd`: the session starts, workspace MCP files and plugins are not loaded (the existing rule), and `session/new` reports `trusted:false` and the count of extensions not loaded in `_meta["nexus/posture"]`. `--require-trusted-workspace` makes it -32602 (D-AC-6).
156	    - Child start failure (non-zero exit before `hello`; `MANAGED_POLICY_EXIT_CODE = 2`, managed_policy_load.ts:41; a config error) gives a `session/new` error -32603 with `data {reason:"sidecar_start_failed", exit_code, message: <redacted stderr tail ≤2,000>}`. No session is created and there is no fallback.
157	    - Once GV-1 wiring exists, the adapter also runs the same loader for the system and user tiers at start and fails `initialize` with -32603 naming file and tier.
158	11. **Untrusted input limits** (constants in `cli/src/acp/types.ts`):
159	
160	| Limit | Value |
161	|---|---|
162	| Inbound line | 4 MiB |
163	| JSON nesting depth (pre-scan outside strings) | 64 |
164	| Text block | 256,000 chars |
165	| Total prompt text | 1,000,000 chars |
166	| Blocks per prompt | 64 |
167	| `cwd`, `sessionId`, URI | 4,096 / 128 / 2,048 chars |
168	| `clientInfo` fields | 100 chars (as `MAX_CLIENT_FIELD`) |
169	| `mcpServers` entries inspected | 32 |
170	| Concurrent sessions | 4 |
171	| In-flight inbound requests | 32 |
172	| Pending permission requests | 1 per session (the sidecar's `approvalTail`) |
173	
174	12. **`cwd` and client strings.**
175	    - `cwd`: a string, absolute, no NUL or newline, `realpathSync`, `statSync().isDirectory()`; the canonical path is what the child gets. Any directory the user can access is accepted and its trust status reported, because a local stdio client already runs as that user.
176	    - Client strings reach only:
177	      - the child's argv: canonical `cwd` and a validated `sessionId`, as array arguments, never a shell
178	      - the prompt text
179	      - stderr logs, through `safeOperatorText`
180	    - Prompt text is the operator's prompt and is unfenced, as in the TUI. No file content passes through the adapter, so the fencing rules for tool output are untouched.
181	
182	## 5. Framing and robustness
183	
184	- **Framing: newline-delimited JSON-RPC 2.0, one object per line, UTF-8.** **V[OC acp.mdx:82-83; OC `packages/cli/src/commands/handlers/acp.ts`:35 (`ndJsonStream`); OC subprocess.ts:276-280, 227-243; HM client:470-474, 499]**. It is not Content-Length framing.
185	- Blank lines are ignored and `\r\n` accepted. Output is `JSON.stringify` plus `\n`, with lone surrogates replaced as `encodeEvent` does (protocol.ts:296-299).
186	- **Correlation.** Inbound requests are answered with their own `id` (string or number; `null` or a fractional id gives -32600). Outbound requests use the registry of §4. A response to an unknown id is dropped and logged.
187	- **Errors.**
188	  - -32700: not JSON, depth exceeded, or oversized, with `id:null`.
189	  - -32600: not an object, a batch, a wrong `jsonrpc`, or not initialised.
190	  - -32601: unknown method. An unknown notification is ignored.
191	  - -32602: validation, with `data.field`.
192	  - -32603: internal or sidecar.
193	  - -32000: auth required.
194	  - -32700 and -32601 are standard JSON-RPC and are used the same way in `cli/src/mcp.ts` and at HM client:680. -32602 and -32603 are **V[OC `packages/cli/test/acp/catalog.test.ts`:30, `error.test.ts`:12]**. **NV**: -32002 "resource not found"; not used.
195	- **Batch** (a top-level array): one -32600 "batch requests are not supported". **NV**: the spec's position.
196	- **Oversized line.** The reader stops buffering at 4 MiB, discards to the next newline, answers -32700 once, and closes the connection after 3 such lines. A child's line over 16 MiB marks that session failed.
197	- **Stdout hygiene.**
198	  - The `acp` action's first statements capture `process.stdout.write`, replace it with a sink, and send `console.log/info/warn/debug` to stderr. This is the pattern of sidecar.ts:1471-1483 and index.ts:543.
199	  - The module imports only node built-ins, `protocol.ts` types and `safe_text.ts`.
200	  - Children's stdout is a pipe the adapter parses; their stderr is forwarded to stderr with a session prefix.
201	  - Test: every stdout line of a real run parses as JSON-RPC.
202	- **EOF and signals.**
203	  - On stdin EOF, SIGTERM, SIGINT or SIGHUP: stop reading, send `shutdown` to each child (which interrupts turns), wait 5 s, SIGTERM, wait 2 s, SIGKILL the child's own pid, exit 0.
204	  - If the adapter is SIGKILLed, each child's stdin closes and the sidecar shuts itself down (sidecar.ts:1517).
205	  - A child that dies unexpectedly: its pending prompt gets -32603, the session is removed, the process keeps serving. Peer precedent for surfacing a dead child: **V[OC `packages/cli/test/acp/lifecycle.subprocess.test.ts`:14-37]**.
206	- **Backpressure.**
207	  - One serial writer; when `write` returns false it waits for `drain` and pauses every child's stdout, so a slow client stalls the sidecar through the pipe instead of growing memory.
208	  - Consecutive `assistant.delta` for one session may be coalesced while paused.
209	  - Queue bound is 8 MiB; beyond it the child stays paused.

**Recommendation: C.**
- The adapter is a pure translator over the sidecar protocol.
- Production uses `ChildSidecarLink`: one sidecar child per ACP session, started with `-w <cwd>` and optionally `-r <id>`. This gives a per-session cwd, several sessions per process (**V[OC `services/www/src/docs/content/cli/acp.mdx`:85-87]** shows a peer serving many sessions from one process), crash isolation, and reuse of the sidecar's own `main()` (lease, state-restore recovery, config, stdout hygiene) unchanged.
- Tests use `InProcessSidecarLink` (a test helper), so nearly every test costs no process start.
- Cost: about 0.65 s at `session/new` from `dist`, and a child-process lifecycle to manage (§5).

**What this means for PF-4.** `ChildSidecarLink` (spawn, typed NDJSON, shutdown) is the "minimal embedding example that spawns the sidecar". Place it at `cli/src/sidecar_client.ts`, importing no commander, so PF-4 only has to export it.

**What this means for VR-2.** The adapter's method table makes a later `_nexus/verify` one entry that calls the `nexus verify` machinery (`cli/src/verify_contract.ts`). AC-1 reserves the name and does not implement it.

**Gaps the sidecar protocol leaves, handled without editing held files**
1. No `call_id` on `approval.request`. Bind to the unique open `tool.start` with the same `turn_id`, `tool` and `subject`; otherwise use a synthetic `toolCallId` `approval-N`. Synthetic ids have precedent: **V[HM `acp_adapter/permissions.py`:81]**.
2. The receipt id exists only as a display row. One function reads the row; a test pins it against `receiptSections`.
3. A failed resume is not structured. Require a `history` event and `session.state.session === requested id`.

An optional later slice adds these three as additive protocol fields (§7, slice 8).

## 4. Permission model

1. **What is asked.** Only a call for which the gate computed `askOperator` (dispatch_tool_call.ts:451-455) and then called `onConfirm` (553). That covers:
   - a write, exec or egress in review mode
   - a first egress per origin in auto mode
   - a command rule `prompt`
   - a verification edit `ask`
   - an injection suspicion
   - a re-issued interrupted call
2. **What is never asked.** Every denial listed in §1, plus read-only mode and the sandbox inside `spine.execute`. These return a `DENIED` receipt without emitting `approval.request`, so the adapter has no pending entry and sends no `session/request_permission`.
3. **Why `allow` cannot override a denial.**
   - The reply enters at exactly one place: `SidecarLink.send({type:"approve", id, always:false})` → `resolveApproval` (sidecar.ts:881).
   - That resolves only the promise of the one open approval whose id matches; anything else is `NO_PENDING_APPROVAL`.
   - After an approval the call still passes `spine.execute` (read-only, sandbox).
   - The adapter has no other verb that affects a tool call.
4. **Binding.** A registry holds `rpcId → {sessionId, approvalId, turnId, toolCallId, digest, state}`.
   - `digest` is the SHA-256 of the canonical `{tool, subject, preview, review}`; it is logged and sent as `toolCall._meta["nexus/approval_digest"]`.
   - A reply carries no content, so it can only answer the request that created its `rpcId`.
   - Outgoing ids are integers from a random 31-bit start (**NV**: whether clients accept string ids), so a response sent before the request exists matches nothing.
5. **Replies that are ignored and logged to stderr, never forwarded.** A tombstone LRU of 256 entries separates stale from unknown.
   - unknown `rpcId`
   - already answered (a second reply)
   - a reply after cancel, turn end or disconnect
   - a response whose `id` is that of a client→agent request
   - a malformed result
6. **Result mapping.**
   - `{outcome:"selected", optionId:"allow_once"}` → `approve`.
   - Everything else → `deny`: `reject_once`, `cancelled`, an option id not offered (**V[HM permissions.py:98-104]** treats an unknown id as deny), `allow_always`, a JSON-RPC error, a wrong type.
   - `always` is the constant `false`. No code path builds `always:true`; a test spies on the link.
7. **Defaults.**
   - No answer within `--permission-timeout` (default 600 s; **V[HM permissions.py:112]** uses 60 s, which is too short for a person in an editor) → `deny`, and the turn continues.
   - Client disconnect, stdin EOF or a signal → shutdown; the sidecar settles the approval false (861).
   - `session/cancel` → the sidecar `cancel` settles it false.
8. **Cancel race.**
   - On `session/cancel` the entry moves to `cancelled` before `cancel` is sent. A later `allow` is stale and ignored.
   - The prompt answers `cancelled` only after `turn.result` arrives.
   - If the approve reached the sidecar first, the tool runs and the abort signal interrupts it. That is the existing TUI behaviour (`cli/test/sidecar.test.ts:351`).
   - The adapter accepts an inbound `$/cancel_request {requestId}` for a prompt request as a cancel (**V[OC turn.ts:390; `packages/cli/test/acp/prompt.test.ts`:495]**).
   - It does not send `$/cancel_request` itself until its spec status is confirmed. **NV**: observed only as SDK behaviour, **V[OC `packages/cli/test/acp/permission.test.ts`:140-144]**.
9. **Mode and trust come from the operator's machine only.**
   - `nexus acp [flags] [-- <sidecar flags>]` forwards operator flags to each child; `-w` and `-r` are refused because the adapter owns them.
   - v1.3.0 allows `--mode review` (default) and `--read-only`. `--yes` and `--mode auto` are refused at start-up with a message (D-AC-3).
   - Trust is read by the child from the trust store. No protocol field, `_meta` key or `clientInfo` value is read for authority.
10. **Untrusted workspace and broken policy.**
    - Untrusted `cwd`: the session starts, workspace MCP files and plugins are not loaded (the existing rule), and `session/new` reports `trusted:false` and the count of extensions not loaded in `_meta["nexus/posture"]`. `--require-trusted-workspace` makes it -32602 (D-AC-6).
    - Child start failure (non-zero exit before `hello`; `MANAGED_POLICY_EXIT_CODE = 2`, managed_policy_load.ts:41; a config error) gives a `session/new` error -32603 with `data {reason:"sidecar_start_failed", exit_code, message: <redacted stderr tail ≤2,000>}`. No session is created and there is no fallback.
    - Once GV-1 wiring exists, the adapter also runs the same loader for the system and user tiers at start and fails `initialize` with -32603 naming file and tier.
11. **Untrusted input limits** (constants in `cli/src/acp/types.ts`):

| Limit | Value |
|---|---|
| Inbound line | 4 MiB |
| JSON nesting depth (pre-scan outside strings) | 64 |
| Text block | 256,000 chars |
| Total prompt text | 1,000,000 chars |
| Blocks per prompt | 64 |
| `cwd`, `sessionId`, URI | 4,096 / 128 / 2,048 chars |
| `clientInfo` fields | 100 chars (as `MAX_CLIENT_FIELD`) |
| `mcpServers` entries inspected | 32 |
| Concurrent sessions | 4 |
| In-flight inbound requests | 32 |
| Pending permission requests | 1 per session (the sidecar's `approvalTail`) |

12. **`cwd` and client strings.**
    - `cwd`: a string, absolute, no NUL or newline, `realpathSync`, `statSync().isDirectory()`; the canonical path is what the child gets. Any directory the user can access is accepted and its trust status reported, because a local stdio client already runs as that user.
    - Client strings reach only:
      - the child's argv: canonical `cwd` and a validated `sessionId`, as array arguments, never a shell
      - the prompt text
      - stderr logs, through `safeOperatorText`
    - Prompt text is the operator's prompt and is unfenced, as in the TUI. No file content passes through the adapter, so the fencing rules for tool output are untouched.

## 5. Framing and robustness

- **Framing: newline-delimited JSON-RPC 2.0, one object per line, UTF-8.** **V[OC acp.mdx:82-83; OC `packages/cli/src/commands/handlers/acp.ts`:35 (`ndJsonStream`); OC subprocess.ts:276-280, 227-243; HM client:470-474, 499]**. It is not Content-Length framing.
- Blank lines are ignored and `\r\n` accepted. Output is `JSON.stringify` plus `\n`, with lone surrogates replaced as `encodeEvent` does (protocol.ts:296-299).
- **Correlation.** Inbound requests are answered with their own `id` (string or number; `null` or a fractional id gives -32600). Outbound requests use the registry of §4. A response to an unknown id is dropped and logged.
- **Errors.**
  - -32700: not JSON, depth exceeded, or oversized, with `id:null`.
  - -32600: not an object, a batch, a wrong `jsonrpc`, or not initialised.
  - -32601: unknown method. An unknown notification is ignored.
  - -32602: validation, with `data.field`.
  - -32603: internal or sidecar.
  - -32000: auth required.
  - -32700 and -32601 are standard JSON-RPC and are used the same way in `cli/src/mcp.ts` and at HM client:680. -32602 and -32603 are **V[OC `packages/cli/test/acp/catalog.test.ts`:30, `error.test.ts`:12]**. **NV**: -32002 "resource not found"; not used.
- **Batch** (a top-level array): one -32600 "batch requests are not supported". **NV**: the spec's position.
- **Oversized line.** The reader stops buffering at 4 MiB, discards to the next newline, answers -32700 once, and closes the connection after 3 such lines. A child's line over 16 MiB marks that session failed.
- **Stdout hygiene.**
  - The `acp` action's first statements capture `process.stdout.write`, replace it with a sink, and send `console.log/info/warn/debug` to stderr. This is the pattern of sidecar.ts:1471-1483 and index.ts:543.
  - The module imports only node built-ins, `protocol.ts` types and `safe_text.ts`.
  - Children's stdout is a pipe the adapter parses; their stderr is forwarded to stderr with a session prefix.
  - Test: every stdout line of a real run parses as JSON-RPC.
- **EOF and signals.**
  - On stdin EOF, SIGTERM, SIGINT or SIGHUP: stop reading, send `shutdown` to each child (which interrupts turns), wait 5 s, SIGTERM, wait 2 s, SIGKILL the child's own pid, exit 0.
  - If the adapter is SIGKILLed, each child's stdin closes and the sidecar shuts itself down (sidecar.ts:1517).
  - A child that dies unexpectedly: its pending prompt gets -32603, the session is removed, the process keeps serving. Peer precedent for surfacing a dead child: **V[OC `packages/cli/test/acp/lifecycle.subprocess.test.ts`:14-37]**.
- **Backpressure.**
  - One serial writer; when `write` returns false it waits for `drain` and pauses every child's stdout, so a slow client stalls the sidecar through the pipe instead of growing memory.
  - Consecutive `assistant.delta` for one session may be coalesced while paused.
  - Queue bound is 8 MiB; beyond it the child stays paused.

## 8. What the release can claim after AC-1 without AC-2

Wording for `docs/ACP.md` and the release notes:

> **Experimental.** `nexus acp` lets a program that speaks the Agent Client Protocol (version 1, newline-delimited JSON-RPC over stdio) drive Nexus: create or load a session, send a prompt, receive streamed text and tool calls with diffs, answer approval requests with allow-once or reject, cancel, and read the verification result and receipt of each turn. It has been tested with a scripted client only. It has not been run against a real ACP client, and it implements a subset: no client-supplied MCP servers, no images or audio, no client file-system or terminal methods, no modes, no session list. Every tool call goes through the same gates as the terminal; an approval reply cannot enable an action the gates deny, and this is tested. Method names and fields may change before the experimental mark is removed.

**Open risks**
1. Every NV item below; the underscore rule and `session_info_update` matter most.
2. Real clients may send non-empty `mcpServers` by default, or may require `messageId` or capabilities Nexus omits.
3. Approval-to-tool-call binding is heuristic until slice 8.
4. Receipts are kept in memory per process.
5. Sessions driven over ACP are recorded with surface `tui` (sidecar.ts:1497).
6. Replay is capped at 60 entries.
7. One child per session costs about 0.65 s and memory.
8. Managed policy is not wired, so the policy-failure path is tested only as "child exits non-zero".
9. The descendants of a SIGKILLed sidecar rely on the sidecar's existing cleanup; the process test will show whether that holds.

**NV list: check against the published specification before relying on it**
- The extension-method naming rule and the name `_nexus/receipt/get`.
- `_meta` placement on every type.
- `session_info_update` in stable v1.
- `max_turn_requests`.
- The `audio` capability key.
- Whether `resource_link` and stdio MCP are mandatory baselines.
- The exact `session/load` response.
- Whether `messageId` is optional.
- The behaviour required before `initialize` and on a repeated `initialize`.
- `$/cancel_request`.
- The batch rule.
- Error code -32002.
- All of `terminal/*`.
- String ids for agent-to-client requests.
- Any message size limit. OC shows the SDK has one (**V[OC `commands/handlers/acp.ts`:39-41]**) but not its value.

/**
 * Operator command rules (CS-9): prefix rules that decide, for a shell command the model wants to run, whether Nexus asks
 * the operator, runs it without asking, or refuses it. Modelled on the data-not-code shape of Codex's `execpolicy`:
 * a three-level outcome (allow < prompt < forbidden), load-time examples that must agree with the rule, and a record of
 * which rule decided.
 *
 *   ~/.config/nexus/command_rules.json (operator home only; a project file is never read)
 *   { "version": 1, "rules": [
 *       { "prefix": ["git", ["status", "log", "diff"]], "decision": "allow", "justification": "read-only git",
 *         "match": ["git status", "git diff --stat"], "notMatch": ["git push"] },
 *       { "prefix": ["git", "push"], "decision": "prompt", "match": ["git push origin main"] },
 *       { "prefix": ["rm", "-rf"], "decision": "forbidden", "justification": "never recursive-delete", "match": ["rm -rf build"] } ] }
 *
 * What a rule can and cannot do:
 * - A rule narrows or widens the *prompt*, never the other controls. Read-only mode, the sandbox, verification-path
 *   protection and the unknown-outcome re-issue gate still apply to a command a rule allows.
 * - `allow` is granted only when every segment of the command (split on `;`, `&&`, `||`, `|`, `&`) matches an allow rule
 *   and the command contains no shell-active character (`$ ` ( ) { } < > * ? !`, a backslash, a newline, or a `~` or `#` that
 *   starts a word) anywhere: a heuristic
 *   never qualifies. A command that cannot be allowed falls back to the normal approval policy.
 * - `prompt` and `forbidden` match any segment, so they cannot be dodged by chaining. Like the destructive-command
 *   tripwire this is a convenience layer, not a sandbox: a command hidden in `$(...)` or a script is not seen, and the
 *   sandbox remains the security boundary.
 * - `forbidden` holds in every mode, including `--yes`. `prompt` holds unless the operator passed `--yes`.
 * - A file that fails to load (bad field, or an example the rules contradict) is refused whole and reported; the normal
 *   approval policy then applies, so a broken file never silently widens or narrows anything.
 */

**REQUEST CHANGES** at head `0c2e33cec87d123f66ff09c1c6b3ff5685595d4d`.

The client-side authority claim held in every experiment I ran: no client value produced an approval, a mode change or trust. The blockers are operator-side and lifecycle defects. My processes are stopped by pid and the worktree is removed.

## Blocking

1. **Auto mode is not refused** (`cli/src/index.ts:1503-1509`). CONFIRMED: `nexus --yes acp`, `--mode auto` and `NEXUS_APPROVAL_MODE=auto` each wrote a file with zero `session/request_permission`; a shell command also ran under the last two. The plan (D-AC-3) refuses these at start-up. Fix: refuse them in the `acp` action.
2. **SIGTERM and SIGINT no longer end the process** (`cli/src/acp_stdio.ts:374-375`). CONFIRMED: idle and mid-turn, the adapter was still alive 12-20 s after the signal and exited only when stdin closed; the children were killed. Fix: `process.exit` after `close()`.
3. **`checkpoint.choice.request` is never answered** (`acp_stdio.ts:289-312`). CONFIRMED: with a private key file in the workspace, the prompt got no update and no reply for 60 s, until `session/cancel`. It never picks a permissive option, but the plan says answer `cancel` with -32603.
4. **Stale approval after `$/cancel_request`** (`acp_stdio.ts:168-175`, `331-332`). CONFIRMED: cancel a prompt with a permission pending, and the next prompt's write is denied with no request sent to the client. Fix: clear `pendingApproval` in that path.

## Non-blocking

5. **No backpressure** (`acp_stdio.ts:59`, `371`). CONFIRMED: with stdout unread, RSS went from 130 MB to 582 MB in 20 s.
6. **After three oversized lines the process stays alive and silent** (`acp_stdio.ts:69`, `75-85`). CONFIRMED.
7. **Sessions are never freed.** CONFIRMED: the 5th session is refused for the life of the connection; `session/close` is -32601.
8. **`always: false` is unguarded by the adapter test.** CONFIRMED: mutating it to `true` at `acp_stdio.ts:109` left the three fake-sidecar tests green. Forcing every matched reply to approve, and removing the session cap, each failed a test.
9. **`acp_stdio.test.ts:13` uses a 10 s deadline for real turns.** CONFIRMED: both real-turn tests failed in 2 of 3 local runs (14-40 s wall) and passed once. CI is green, and an existing sidecar test is equally slow here, so this is host latency exposing a tight deadline.
10. **Docs.** Reading only: the help text and `docs/ACP.md` do not say "experimental" (only `initialize` does); `docs/PROTOCOL.md:15` still says "No Agent Client Protocol"; the stdio-MCP deviation is not stated as a spec deviation; `loadSession: true` with partial replay is documented accurately, but not advertising it would be more honest.

## Held up when run

- **(a) Read-only:** unsolicited allow results had no effect; no request, no file.
- **(b) Permission replies:** `allow_always`, an unoffered id, a JSON-RPC error, wrong types and reject-then-allow all denied; a string id was ignored. `allow_once` with extra `always: true` fields approved once and the next write asked again.
- **Gates:** forbidden command rule, verification `block` mode and forbidden deletion sent no request and took no effect. Default verification mode asks, and allow-once then permits the edit.
- **(c) `cwd`:** relative, file, missing and newline are refused; a symlink or any outside directory is accepted, as the plan intends. Client MCP servers were not started and were reported.
- **Load:** `latest`, a prefix and another workspace's session are refused; same-workspace load replays.
- **(e) Framing:** a 256 MiB line peaked RSS at 204 MB; depth bomb, batch, malformed JSON, pre- and repeated `initialize` are answered correctly.
- **(f) EOF mid-turn:** exit 0 in 7.4 s, `sleep` and `harness-core` gone.
- **Late allow after `session/cancel`:** no write.
- **Stdout:** every line parsed in all runs.
- **Managed policy:** start-up load and clamps apply (reading only).

## Tests

- The other four `acp_*` files passed 3 of 3 (53 tests, under 3.2 s each).
- `acp_stdio.test.ts` does not cover real approvals, cancel races, timeout, EOF, signals, framing, `cwd`, checkpoint choice or auto mode.

## Not checked

- Head-versus-base failing sets, and the `index.ts` help and command suites (stopped first).
- The load id-match mutation (the run hung and I killed it).
- The 10-minute timeout, Node 22, real clients, and the unhandled-rejection path from `finishPrompt`.
